_note: Stress scenarios are stored as the INDEX LEVELS they are derived from, not as a percentage. The percentage is recomputed from the levels at load time and a test asserts the arithmetic. That way the only thing anyone has to verify is two published closing prices, and correcting a level corrects every number downstream of it in one place. A magnitude asserted directly as '-38%' cannot be checked at all.
_verification: Every level below is transcribed from published index closing prices. Transcription is a step where errors happen, so the status field says so. Re-verify against your data provider before quoting any of these in an interview - and if a level is wrong, fix it here, not in the code.

scenarios.name: gfc_2008_calendar_year
scenarios.label: Global Financial Crisis - S&P 500 calendar year 2008
scenarios.note: This is the figure usually quoted as '2008 was down about 38%'. It is a calendar-year price return and it is NOT the same thing as the crisis drawdown - the index fell considerably further peak to trough. Quoting one and describing the other is the most common sloppiness in this area.

scenarios.name: gfc_peak_to_trough
scenarios.label: Global Financial Crisis - S&P 500 peak to trough
scenarios.note: The full drawdown, 17 months from the October 2007 closing high to the March 2009 closing low. This is the number a risk committee cares about, because it is what an investor holding through the crisis actually experienced.

scenarios.name: covid_crash_2020
scenarios.label: COVID-19 crash - S&P 500, Feb-Mar 2020
scenarios.note: 23 trading days from record close to trough - a comparable magnitude to the 2008 calendar year compressed into five weeks. Speed matters as much as depth for a portfolio with any liquidity constraint, which a single-shock model does not capture.

scenarios.name: gfc_2008_calendar_year_nifty
scenarios.label: Global Financial Crisis - NIFTY 50 calendar year 2008
scenarios.source: NIFTY 50 published daily closing levels (NSE India)
scenarios.note: Indian equities fell materially harder than US equities in 2008 despite the crisis originating in US housing credit - a useful reminder that a portfolio's crisis exposure is about capital flows and risk appetite, not only about where the shock started.

scenarios.name: gfc_peak_to_trough_nifty
scenarios.label: Global Financial Crisis - NIFTY 50 peak to trough
scenarios.source: NIFTY 50 published daily closing levels (NSE India)
scenarios.note: Closing high to closing low. Intraday levels are higher and lower respectively; closes are used throughout this project so that every figure comes off the same series the returns are computed from.

scenarios.name: covid_crash_2020_nifty
scenarios.label: COVID-19 crash - NIFTY 50, Jan-Mar 2020
scenarios.source: NIFTY 50 published daily closing levels (NSE India)
scenarios.note: The NIFTY bottomed on the same session as the S&P 500. In a global liquidity event correlations converge towards one, which is precisely when a diversification assumption fitted on calm-period data stops holding.
